newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Virgin boss in Morocco to prepare balloon bid. [CORRECTED 09:15 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Virgin boss in Morocco to prepare balloon bid. [CORRECTED 09:15 GMT]

text.p: British tycoon Richard Branson arrived in Morocco late on Friday to prepare for another attempt to be first to fly round the world by balloon.

Branson, with one of his two co-pilots for the attempt, arrived in his small private jet at the civil airport in the central Moroccan city of Marrakesh (corrects to make clear that only one co-pilot arrived with Branson).
He told reporters: "I am here for the weekend to train on the balloon."
His plans were to return to Britain on Monday but if the weather was promising he said he might stay to start the attempt next week.
"But it will definitely be before the end of January, depending on the weather," he added.
Branson and co-pilots Per Linstrand, who built the prototype balloon, and hang-gliding champion Rory McCarthy, aim to be first to fly by balloon round the world and expect to do it in about 18 days.

The British entrepreneur, who has brushed with death twice on record-breaking balloon flights, faces a race from American balloonist Steve Fosset and a two-man team planning a launch from Switzerland.

Last January, Branson had to abandon an attempt from the airbase in Marrakesh because of the weather. The 45-year-old boss of the Virgin group of companies, as he waited for right weather conditions, then termed the attempt a "mad adventure".
